loci.name: fleet-service-model-by-host-class
loci.one_line: How does ONE agent codebase and ONE NixOS module actually serve all 7 jupiterOS hosts — user-service-with-linger on kiosks/desktops vs system-service-with-capabilities on headless boxes — covering unit lifecycle (the nixos-rebuild user-unit restart gap), D-Bus access (/run/user/<uid>/bus reachability from a system service), privileges, and double-registration avoidance?
loci.rationale: Merged from analyst-A 'service-model-for-every-host' and analyst-B 'fleet-service-model-by-host-class' (same core question, both top-scored). This IS the 'every host in jupiterOS' question; the contradiction graph admits it 'reconciles by host-class, not by winner' but no source designs the split. Open depth questions: (a) the shape of a services.ha-agent module shipping a system unit on europa/pallene/callisto and a lingered user unit on kiosks via mkIf; (b) whether a system service with User=io can reach the session bus at /run/user/<uid>/bus (which exists under linger without a graphical session); (c) verifying the nixos-rebuild-switch user-unit restart gap is still true on current NixOS (thread is Feb 2023); (d) how credentials/TLS reach the agent per host (tls knob verified dead in config.rs:88); (e) SMART AmbientCapabilities vs the existing sysfs-chmod workaround's interaction.

opposing_positions.position: User service + linger everywhere: no root, session bus free for niri/notifications, go-hass-agent refuses root, jupiter-os ships ConditionUser=io+linger today

System service (User=/AmbientCapabilities=) at least on servers: user units don't restart on nixos-rebuild switch, can't order after system units, 9-year declarative-linger gap, SMART capabilities only grantable on system units, 'No medium found' bus maze headless

suggested_searches: system service connect to session dbus /run/user bus User=
NixOS systemd.user.services restart nixos-rebuild switch current

loci.name: mqtt-lifecycle-supervisor-spec
loci.one_line: What is the concrete, implementable MQTT lifecycle supervisor design on rumqttc — re-subscribe on every ConnAck, clean_session=false + stable client_id, birth-message-triggered discovery republish with jitter, LWT + explicit SIGTERM offline publish, stale-message bounding, ghost cleanup via empty-payload publishes, per-backend task isolation (fixes the verified hung-syncthing stall), and the paired broker max_queued_messages sizing on callisto — mapped defect-by-defect to the file:line audit?
loci.rationale: Merged from analyst-A 'mqtt-lifecycle-state-machine' and analyst-B 'mqtt-lifecycle-supervisor-spec'. The user's 'never reliable' complaint is the research centre of gravity; the WHAT is near-consensus (consensus-claims.json) but the HOW is unassembled: rumqttc has no disconnect callback and no pending TTL (#211, open since 2020); HA docs recommend a random delay on birth-triggered rediscovery; Z2M's production jitter/backoff pattern (30s jitter, x1.5-x12 backoff) is the reference; broker max_queued_messages (mosquitto default 1000) silently dropped 56/112 retained topics at HA #135266's 5374-entity scale — the spec must pair agent behaviour with callisto's actual mosquitto config; rumqttc at main is v3.1.1-only so HA's message_expiry_interval is unavailable and ghost cleanup must use Homie's empty-payload order; the retained-discipline matrix (config+state+availability retained, commands never) is corpus-established.
suggested_searches: MQTT client supervisor pattern stale message TTL
HA mqtt discovery cleanup empty payload remove device

loci.name: adopt-vs-build-honest-verdict
loci.one_line: Given go-hass-agent v14.15.1 is already in nixpkgs and lnxlink is community-endorsed with ~50 modules, is improving ha-linux-agent the right call at all — and if yes, exactly which jupiterOS-native capabilities (launcher mutual-exclusion groups, kiosk session switching, ZFS/headscale backends, declarative NixOS module, single-device MQTT-only identity) justify the maintenance burden of a 12-crate workspace with 3 tests — including the notification-transport fork (MQTT-only vs native-API for actionable notifications) that decides the feature table?
loci.rationale: Merged from analyst-A 'adopt-vs-build-honest-verdict' + analyst-B 'adopt-vs-build-verdict' + analyst-A's 'transport-mqtt-only-vs-dual' folded in (the actionable-notifications fork is a feature of the comparison table, and analyst-B skip-justified the broader transport fight as resolved-for-this-fleet). The user said 'improve it' but an advocate-register report must argue improve-vs-adopt or its roadmap is question-begging. Unresolved: the feature-by-feature delta table against go-hass-agent's full catalogue and lnxlink's ~50 modules; whether the incumbents work headless on servers (verify against their issue trackers); whether their lack of a NixOS service module (package only) is sufficient differentiation; and what is/isn't possible over MQTT discovery alone for notifications (halinuxcompanion needs a local HTTP server, go-hass-agent the native websocket, lnxlink carries them over MQTT — ha-linux-agent's notify backend has no documented HA→host delivery path at all today).

opposing_positions.position: Adopt: mature agent already in nixpkgs, monthly releases, sensor-complete, security-mature; lnxlink community-endorsed; ha-linux-agent's differentiation is small against a 12-crate workspace with 3 tests and a failing clippy gate

Build/fix: launcher mutual-exclusion groups for kiosk/gaming session switching, ZFS/headscale backends, first-class declarative NixOS module, MQTT-only single-device identity avoiding go-hass-agent's documented split-brain (device under TWO HA integrations)

suggested_searches: go-hass-agent headless server no desktop session
home assistant mqtt notify actionable notifications device

loci.name: headless-privilege-ladder
loci.one_line: For the server hosts (europa, pallene, callisto), which monitoring channel + privilege design per subsystem — SMART via smartd -M exec hooks vs CAP_SYS_ADMIN/CAP_SYS_RAWIO ioctls, ZFS via zed events vs zpool polling, systemd unit health via D-Bus signals vs OnFailure= drop-in, backlight via udev uevents vs sysfs polling — and what capability set does the resulting unit need?
loci.rationale: Merged from analyst-A 'jupiteros-sensor-privilege-matrix' + analyst-B 'headless-privilege-ladder' + analyst-A's 'poll-vs-event-hybrid' fragments absorbed (B's absorption rationale). Per-subsystem channel+privilege design is genuinely open and feeds back into the service-model locus. Kernel-source evidence: NVMe SMART REQUIRES CAP_SYS_ADMIN (NVME_IOCTL_ADMIN_CMD), SATA needs CAP_SYS_RAWIO; zpool unprivileged-readability is an audited absence worth a hard search; zbus system-bus unit-state subscription vs the global OnFailure=failure-handler@%N drop-in pattern; niri's event stream for kiosk state; udev uevents for backlight hotkey sync.

loci.name: rumqttc-dependency-fitness
loci.one_line: Is rumqttc (pinned 0.24 here) the right dependency to build the reliability phase on: is re-subscription (#250, labelled in-pipeline as #1052) actually fixed in any release, what is the crate's real maintenance state, and does its MQTT v3.1.1-only surface force the lifecycle spec's workarounds — or should the agent switch clients?
loci.rationale: Analyst-B unique. Every phase-1 fix builds on rumqttc yet the corpus never verifies it's the right bet: #250 open since Feb 2021 labelled 'in-pipeline as of #1052' — no evidence PR #1052 or any release shipped re-subscription handling; 0.25.1 docs built Sept 2026 (alive) but only 35.34% documented; #211 (no disconnect callback, no TTL) open/stale since 2020; main-branch is v3.1.1-only (mqttbytes::v4), locking out HA's message_expiry_interval; what changed 0.24→0.25.1; what alternatives (paho.mqtt.rust etc.) look like against the supervisor requirements; mosquitto v2.0.12+ requires non-zero keep-alive (#2117). Keep-vs-replace changes phase-1 implementation cost and the roadmap's credibility.
suggested_searches: rust MQTT client production paho vs rumqttc

loci.rationale: Analyst-B unique; analyst-A skip-noted it as implementation detail but conceded it's phase-gating. Without it the roadmap's 'reliability first' phase has no definition of done.
